title: 12 DIY Thanksgiving Centerpiece Ideas for Every Table
summary: Whether you're keeping it cozy or having people over, these easy and beautiful Thanksgiving table centerpieces are a sight to behold.

# 12 DIY Thanksgiving Centerpiece Ideas for Every Table


-
-
-


24 November 2026


[Beth Baty](https://cricut.com/blog/author/bethb/)


Bring a handmade touch to your Thanksgiving gathering with a seasonal centerpiece.


---


A Thanksgiving centerpiece gives everyone something special to gather around. It could be a tray filled with pumpkins, a box overflowing with fall flowers, or a colorful paper arrangement you can bring out year after year; either way, a few handmade details make it feel like yours.


DIY Thanksgiving centerpieces can be modified to fit any aesthetic and guest list, with fun touches such as rustic pumpkin trays, paper leaves on dried branches, paper flowers, personalized pumpkins, decorated candle displays, and kid-friendly gratitude trees. Start with a tray, vase, or candle, then use your Cricut cutting machine to add seasonal paper flowers, pumpkins, leaves, or decorative lettering to suit your table.


Whether you love warm harvest colors or want to try a softer palette, these 13 ideas offer a starting point for a Cricut Thanksgiving centerpiece that suits any celebration. Plus, all of these ideas are simply a starting place! Feel free to swap out color schemes, exact lettering, and seasonal motifs to fit your personal Thanksgiving table.


## Rustic and Farmhouse Thanksgiving Centerpieces


Woven textures, warm wood, and fall floral arrangements give these centerpieces their cozy farmhouse feel. The handmade details are small, but they help pull the whole display together.


### 1. “Give Thanks” wood flower box


A wooden box filled with yellow and white sunflowers or other fall florals makes for a friendly, bright focal point on a farmhouse table.


Recreate this look by using your Cricut cutting machine to cut out “Give Thanks” or a similar seasonal phrase from white vinyl. Then use Transfer Tape to apply the phrase onto a smooth, finished wood box. Keep the lettering centered on the front of the box and arrange the flowers so they frame the words without covering them. The box’s long shape works especially well along a rectangular or buffet table and would really pop with a table runner underneath!


#### **Suggested materials:**


- A Cricut cutting machine with a compatible LightGrip or StandardGrip machine mat
- Long wooden planter box with a smooth, finished front
- White permanent vinyl
- Transfer tape
- Weeding tool
- Scraper tool
- Faux sunflowers


### 2. Acorn-accented vase with sunflowers


For a super simple rustic centerpiece that will still stand out, add some acorn and oak leaf embellishments to a porcelain vase and fill the vase with fall flowers! The simple white base can match your everyday dishes and silverware, while the vinyl embellishment adds a fall touch to bring your Thanksgiving aesthetic to life.


Find this[Fall Canvas Texture Ceramic Vase](https://design.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/5bbb3f93ce733d061a34f079) design on Design Space and use permanent vinyl in fall colors to achieve a similar end result. Pair this centerpiece with a burlap runner and a few pinecones or scattered leaves for a cozy woodland feel. It’s an easy way to bring natural textures and warm autumn colors to the table without needing an elaborate arrangement.


#### **Suggested materials:**


- White ceramic vase
- Yellow, orange, red, light brown, and brown permanent vinyl
- Transfer tape
- Weeding tool
- Scraper tool
- Faux sunflowers bouquet
- Optional: Burlap runner
- Optional: Decorative leaves, pinecones, acorns, and woven twig balls


### 3. Paper apple basket with autumn flowers


A paper apple basket filled with fall flowers brings a cozy, harvest-inspired feel to your Thanksgiving table. Its cream-and-gray palette pairs easily with neutral linens, wood accents, and everyday dishes, making it a natural fit for farmhouse or rustic gatherings.


The basket gives the bouquet a handmade touch, while loosely arranged fall flowers and greenery keep it feeling natural and welcoming. It’s a great choice for a table that feels thoughtfully styled without being too formal.


To recreate the look, assemble the paper basket around a separate vase using the[3D Apple Basket](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/58a64021e64add320a6289fe) design from Design Space. If you’re using fresh flowers, be extra careful to keep the water inside your inner vase so it won’t touch the cardstock.


#### **Suggested materials:**


- Cream and gray cardstock
- Craft glue
- Floral vase (should be small enough to fit inside of your paper basket)
- Autumn bouquet


### 4. “Happy Thanksgiving” wood sign with harvest accents


Let a warm message take center stage with a wood “Happy Thanksgiving” sign! This sign gives your centerpiece a clear focal point, and its warm wood tones and classic fall colors suit rustic, farmhouse, or traditional Thanksgiving gatherings. Pair it with a few small pumpkins and natural accents for a cozy harvest feel.


Recreate the look by using the[Happy Thanksgiving Wood Sign](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/59dd3d8d471f1605651c2c31) from Design Space. Use a display stand for the sign, or prop the sign against a wall if you’ve got a buffet-style serving table for Thanksgiving.


#### **Suggested materials:**


- Smooth, finished, blank rectangular wood sign
- Black (or dark brown) and orange permanent vinyl
- Transfer tape
- Weeding tool
- Scraper tool
- Optional: Display stand
- Optional: Small pumpkins, decorative leaves, pinecones, nuts, and woven twig balls


## Blue and White Thanksgiving Centerpieces


A blue-and-white palette offers a fresh way to style a fall table. Carry those colors into the paper details of your centerpiece, then repeat them in your linens and other table decor.


### 5. Minimalist dangling leaf centerpiece


Crafting a table setting in blues and whites with gold or bronze accents is a trendy way to create a brighter, cleaner take on a Thanksgiving spread. This centerpiece creates a crisp and classy vibe for anyone who would rather step away from the classic deep colors of autumn.


To make your own blue-and-white centerpiece, pair the main[Leaf Centerpiece](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/57563e3eee508efa43323228) project and a small[Autumn Colors Framed Art](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/57563e46ee508efa4332322e) project from Design Space. Choose a clear glass vase and keep your branches tall and thin with a minimal amount of dangling leaves in deep blue and bronze; that way your guests can still see each other around the centerpiece.


#### Suggested materials:


- Deep blue, bronze or gold, and white cardstock
- Gold or bronze permanent vinyl
- Transfer tape
- Weeding tools
- Scraper tool
- Small frame
- Clear glass vase
- Long, thin dried branches
- Tape or white string


### 6. Paper floral arrangement with white candles


For another fresh take on Thanksgiving decor, pair cream, deep blue, and green paper flowers with white candles and natural beige accents. Adding green florals to your white-and-blue color scheme bridges the palette, adding a natural touch that keeps the cooler colors feeling warm and welcoming.


To make this[Floral Centerpiece](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/575660c6ee508efa43329314) , follow the directions on Design Space. Choose cardstock in cream, deep blue, soft sage, and yellow-green, then arrange your paper flowers in a low ceramic bowl. Bring in a matching shade of blue through your napkins, table runner, or the bowl itself, and finish with natural light wood accents and white candles for a soft Thanksgiving glow.


#### Suggested materials:


- Deep blue, cream, soft sage, and yellow-green cardstock
- Cricut machine scoring tool
- Hot glue gun and glue sticks
- Tweezers
- Ceramic bowl (I suggest a deep blue or cream/white one)
- Floral Foam
- Floral Wire Stems
- Gauge Wire, 18
- Wire Cutters
- White candles
- Optional: Wood accents


## Pumpkin and Acorn Centerpieces


### 7. Rustic pumpkin tray with paper leaves


Bring the harvest to the table with a rectangular woven tray filled with colorful pumpkins, small wood rounds for leveling, warm orange and yellow candles, burlap wraps, and scattered paper leaves and acorns.


To recreate the look, start with the largest gourds, then fit the smaller accents around them. Choose battery-operated candles when styling beside paper, burlap, and dried decorative materials. Use the[Fall Centerpiece](https://design.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/575657b3ee508efa43327843) project from Design Space to create the leaf and branch cutouts featured in this centerpiece. Combine store-bought candles and pumpkins with the Cricut-cut leaves, or swap out the store-bought pieces for some[3D paper pumpkins](https://design.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/58a640271d31ac7c0b61b94d) for a fully handcrafted display.


#### Suggested materials:


- Rectangular woven tray
- Small decorative pumpkins
- Wood rounds
- Falll colored candles
- Burlap ribbon
- Decorative acorns
- Cardstock in fall colors


### 8. Paper acorn and pinecone lantern


This clear glass lantern filled with 3D paper acorns and pinecones brings a fun woodland feel to your Thanksgiving table. The enclosed arrangement keeps the small pieces gathered neatly, making it easy to move when it’s time to serve dinner or clean up and store for next year.


To make your own, follow the[Acorn and Pinecone Lantern](https://design.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/57563d87ee508efa433230f3) project instructions on Design Space to cut and assemble the cardstock and vellum pieces, then arrange them inside a lantern, jar, or cloche. Use one larger lantern as a focal point, or group a few smaller lanterns in two or three sections along the center of the table for a coordinated look that reaches across the whole table.


#### **Suggested materials:**


- A Cricut cutting machine with a compatible LightGrip machine mat
- Brown, kraft, light kraft, and orange cardstock
- Metallic vellum
- Cricut machine scoring tool
- Hot glue gun and glue sticks
- Lantern


### 9. Paper 3D pumpkins and pumpkin pie slice


Three-dimensional paper pumpkins and a paper pie slice bring a playful handmade touch to your Thanksgiving table. They’re a natural fit for a relaxed family gathering, adding harvest charm in colors you can coordinate with your dishes and linens. Plus, you can save the finished pieces to enjoy again next year.


To make your own, open the[3D Pumpkins](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/58a640271d31ac7c0b61b94d) and[Pumpkin Pie Box](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/58a63fe2719e813b7e31dda2) designs in Design Space, cut the pieces from cardstock, and follow the project instructions for scoring, folding, and assembly. Group them with a few pumpkins or other gourds for added texture, keeping the arrangement low enough for conversation.


#### Suggested materials:


- Cream, green, light green, dark gray-green, orange, and pumpkin-colored cardstock
- Gold metallic poster board
- Weeder
- Cricut machine scoring tool
- Hot glue gun and glue sticks


## Budget Centerpieces from Thrifted Finds


Thrifted vases, candleholders, and candlesticks make a great starting point for a personalized Thanksgiving centerpiece. A few paper details or custom stickers can bring mismatched finds together, giving your table a coordinated look without buying a whole new set of decorations.


### 10. Floral paper candle wrap


Give a thrifted white LED pillar candle a makeover with this super simple paper candle wrap. The delicate cutouts add texture, while the candle’s glow brings a soft, welcoming atmosphere to the table. Choose warm brown or copper-toned cardstock for a rustic Thanksgiving setting, or cream for a softer, understated look.


To make your own candle wrap, first be sure to measure around each candle, then size the[Floral Candle Wrap](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/57929104212426ff3e6c37e0) in Design Space to fit, allowing a little overlap for fastening it together at the end.


As a note here, while you could use a real burning candle for this project, I suggest getting an LED one if you plan on actually having the candle “burn” during your dinner; that way you don’t need to worry about your candle shrinking throughout the night or catching fire to the paper wrap.


#### Suggested materials:


- A Cricut cutting machine with a compatible LightGrip machine mat
- Brown pearl paper or kraft paper
- Cricut machine scoring tool
- Craft glue or tape
- LED pillar candle


### 11. Celestial Candle Votive Stickers


Turn secondhand glass votive holders into a sparkling centerpiece with this project! The holographic finish catches the light, adding a festive shimmer that suits a warm and cozy gathering or a Thanksgiving table with other metallic accents and silverware. Use these star stickers across all of the different glass shapes you find to make your thrifted collection feel intentional.


To make your own, follow the steps found on Design Space for the[Celestial Candle Votive Stickers](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/68c986d0d9049cf98384a46b) . Don’t forget to start by cleaning and drying your glass votives; that way the adhesive sticks to the glass surface without any bubbling. Add some candles of varying sizes and shapes to your votives and place the finished pieces in groups of three across your table, or place two or three votives on a matching metallic tray directly in the center of the table for an easy-to-move centerpiece.


#### Suggested materials:


- A Cricut cutting machine with Print then Cut functionality
- Compatible LightGrip machine mat
- [Printable Waterproof Holographic Sticker Set – US Letter](https://cricut.com/en-us/materials/material-type/vinyl/printable-waterproof-holographic-sticker-set---us-letter-5-ct/2011886.html)
- InkJet Printer


## Kid-Friendly Thanksgiving Centerpieces


Get the kids involved in decorating with pre-cut paper leaves and a few simple supplies. Prepare the paper leaves ahead of time using your Cricut cutting machine, then invite all your little makers to write, draw, and help assemble as they wait for food on Thanksgiving Day! Find more kids’ projects to make together in our[Thanksgiving crafts guide](https://cricut.com/blog/guide-to-thanksgiving-crafts/) .


### 12. Colorful paper leaf and branch arrangement


Bring fall color indoors with a gratitude tree centerpiece! Before your guests arrive, use your Cricut cutting machine to prepare the paper leaves. Set the pre-cut leaves across the table with markers and pens, and arrange the dried branches in a vase in the center of the table.


Then comes the fun part! Invite everyone —adults and kids alike — to write or draw something they’re grateful for on a leaf, then use a small piece of tape to stick the leaf to one of the dried branches. Little ones can dictate their thoughts to an adult or doodle a picture. As the leaves fill up, the centerpiece becomes a beautiful fall tree that also serves as a shared reminder of the people and moments everyone appreciates.


To make it, use the leaf shapes found on the[Leaf and Branch Centerpiece](https://design-beta.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/575638f6ee508efa43322550) project in Design Space. Secure a few branches in a stable vase or low container, then use your Cricut cutting machine to cut the maple leaves in varying fall colors.


#### Suggested materials:


- A Cricut cutting machine with a compatible LightGrip machine mat
- Yellow, orange, and red cardstock
- Clear tape
- Several dried sticks and twigs
- Vase
- Markers and pens


## How to Make a Thanksgiving Centerpiece


For this guide, I’ll be using the rustic pumpkin tray centerpiece inspired by project #7. The pumpkins and woven textures do most of the decorating, while the paper leaves add a fun handmade accent without being too labor-intensive.


### 1. Gather your materials


Find or buy a shallow woven tray, two decorative pumpkins or other gourds, three small wood rounds, three small orange and warm yellow candles, one large orange or warm yellow pillar candle, burlap ribbon, and decorative acorns. Next, pick out cardstock in mustard, rust, tan, and muted green for the paper leaves and greenery.


You’ll also need your Cricut cutting machine, a compatible blade and mat, and adhesive for the paper accents. For help choosing supplies, read[how to pick the right Cricut material for your project](https://cricut.com/blog/how-to-pick-the-right-cricut-material-for-your-project/) .


### 2. Cut the paper leaves out


Cut the leaves out, following the directions found in the[Fall Centerpiece](https://design.cricut.com/landing/project-detail/575657b3ee508efa43327843) project on Design Space. Check the size of the leaves to be sure they’ll complement your pumpkins and candles, then follow the on-screen prompts to cut them from cardstock using the appropriate material settings. Once they’re cut, gently lift the cut pieces from the mat, taking extra care with the slender stems.


### 3. Build your base


Place your tray on the center of your table and add the pumpkins near the center and back of the woven tray. Arrange the small wood rounds toward the front and sides to create spots for the candles. Keep each support level and stable (you can also use hot glue to hold the wood and candles in place better).


### 4. Add the handmade details


Wrap your candles with burlap, then add a few paper leaves to the wraps. Then, tuck the remaining paper leaves near the pumpkin stems or scattered across the middle of the table. And finally, place the leafy paper sprigs between the larger elements.


### 5. Style the finished tray


At last, add the decorative acorns scattered around the tray and table. Be sure to leave some of the bottom of the woven tray visible so the arrangement doesn’t feel crowded! Set your centerpiece on the table, sit down, and check that the centerpiece leaves room for conversation and serving dishes, and then you’re ready to go!


Wondering what the traditional Thanksgiving centerpiece is called? It’s a cornucopia, or horn of plenty, and it’s normally portrayed as a horn-shaped basket often filled with fall harvest produce.


## How to Choose a Centerpiece Size and Color Palette


Let your table guide the size of your centerpiece. For example, a long flower box suits a long rectangular table, while a compact bowl of paper flowers works well on a round table. Plus, a tray under your centerpiece elements can make a layered arrangement that’s easier to move if you need extra space for the actual meal.


Keep your dining-table arrangements short if you don’t plan on moving them before eating; that way, your guests can still see one another while sitting around the table. Twelve inches or shorter is a pretty good starting height, but always check from your actual seats before building out the whole centerpiece.


To pick a color theme, look at the dishes and linens you already have and try to match those colors in your centerpiece and accents. Classic fall colors are always a hit, and accent colors in gold and creams can tie things together. Carry the same colors into your[Thanksgiving table decor](https://cricut.com/blog/thanksgiving-crafts-with-cricut/) , or explore[Create the perfect dinner party tablescape](https://cricut.com/blog/dinner-party-tablescape-inspiration/) for more styling inspiration.


You can also keep costs down by reusing a tray, vase, or planter you already have for your centerpiece. And as far as time goes, focus your crafting time on the detail that makes the biggest difference, whether that’s paper leaves, layered flowers, or vinyl lettering.


## Get started on your centerpiece


Ready to make your centerpiece personal? Download or open[Design Space](https://design.cricut.com/?visitorId=b10e1f51-4d26-47f2-a3f4-52a125918d43&deepLinkGuid=4a1506d6-46d2-4088-9182-d3807fa9845a) to find designs for the paper leaves, baskets, flowers, pumpkins, acorns, and lettering that bring your arrangement together. Then finish the setting with coordinating[Thanksgiving table decor](https://cricut.com/blog/thanksgiving-crafts-with-cricut/) , from place cards to napkin rings.


## Thanksgiving Centerpiece FAQs


####


The best Thanksgiving centerpiece suits your table and leaves room for guests and food. A rustic pumpkin tray is a versatile choice, while a paper floral arrangement adds handmade detail you can reuse. Choose colors and materials that work with your dishes and linens.


####


Start with a tray, bowl, or planter. Add your main element, such as pumpkins or flowers, then fill smaller spaces with leaves or acorns. Finish with a handmade detail, such as paper leaves or vinyl lettering, and check the view from each seat.


####


Use a container you already own, then choose a few seasonal elements to fill it. Arrange gourds in a woven tray, fill a wood box with fall flowers, or build a paper fall bouquet in a ceramic bowl. Repeat a few colors to bring the arrangement together.


####


A traditional Thanksgiving centerpiece is a cornucopia, also known as a horn of plenty. It’s a horn-shaped basket filled with harvest items such as fruits and vegetables. Pumpkin displays, floral arrangements, and handmade paper decorations are other popular choices.


####


A centerpiece on the dining table should stay low enough for seated guests to see one another comfortably. Around 12 inches or less is a helpful starting point. Check the arrangement from your seats and move taller displays to a sideboard if they block conversation.


####


Try a group of pumpkins with one vinyl-lettered focal pumpkin, a tray of gourds with cut-paper leaves, a vase of dried branches and hanging paper leaves, or a wood planter filled with faux fall flowers. 3D paper pumpkins and layered paper flowers are options when you’d like to spend more time crafting.


####


Combine warm wood or woven textures with pumpkins and autumn colors. A rustic woven tray goes well with pumpkins and wood rounds, burlap, acorns, and paper leaves as accents. A dark wood box with white “Give Thanks” lettering and fall flowers is another farmhouse-inspired option.


####


Start with a tray, vase, or bowl you already own and reuse seasonal decorations from previous years. Add paper leaves cut from cardstock scraps or personalize an existing planter with vinyl lettering. Dress up thrifted glass with leaf details, or pair candles with secondhand candleholders, which you can elevate with simple vinyl decals or transparent stickers. A smaller arrangement needs fewer supplies and leaves more room on the table.
